title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Kenny Clarke - Swing to Bop' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 23 April 2022)
notes: Two pages, 91 bars from 'the last ten beats of the first A section' of Christian's solo, marked 220. Brushes; 'a strong quarter note groove, with Clarke making some big angular jabs with the snare drum and bass drum'; the cymbal and hi-hat 'mics barely register'; 'You can assume that he's feathering the bass drum throughout'; the running eighths 'a swing pattern with the left hand in the gap'. PDF: pdxdrummer.com. Read bar by bar.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Kenny Clarke fours' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 12 March 2015)
notes: Love Me or Leave Me, Miles Davis, Walkin' (Prestige): 'drum fours only - starting at 4:39', the half note at 145, brushes. Eight fours. The ties 'likely reflect left-hand activity'; the quintuplet lick 'probably contains a double', 'likely conceived as two eighth notes and a triplet slurred together'. Read bar by bar from the image.

title: Todd Bishop, 'Transcription: Kenny Clarke fours - 02' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 29 October 2019)
notes: Two Not One, Lee Konitz with Warne Marsh (Atlantic): 'trading fours starting at 3:55', marked 238, sticks. 'Clarke doesn't play the tom toms at all'; the recurring triplet lick in paradiddle sticking from the left hand; five-stroke rolls and double paradiddles; stick shots; four-stroke ruffs a 'flash lick'. Read bar by bar from the PDF.

title: Todd Bishop, 'The Kenny Note' (Cruise Ship Drummer!, 8 July 2012)
notes: 'Clarke really favors comping with the snare drum on the & of 1 and/or 3'; from Apothegm, Jazzmen: Detroit (Savoy): a two-measure phrase repeated in the first 16 bars of the head, and the second 16 bars transcribed; the same punctuation behind soloists. No tempo given. Read bar by bar from the PDF.

title: Miles Davis - Bags' Groove (Songsterr drum tab)
notes: Human transcription (aiGenerated false), revision 396617, by gianluca aculnaig (2020). Marks 140; 242 bars: two of cross-stick, then twenty choruses of the blues. The take is not named; both takes' previews autocorrelate at 146. The swung ride written as dotted values.

title: Thelonious Monk Discography (jazzdisco.org)
notes: Lists Swing to Bop at Minton's Playhouse, 12 May 1941, Charlie Christian and Kenny Clarke with Nick Fenton; issued on Esoteric ESJ-1. The pianist is disputed: other sources give Kenny Kersey, and Joe Guy on trumpet.

title: Charlie Christian - Wikipedia
notes: Jerry Newman's 1941 recordings at Minton's on a portable disk recorder, Christian with Joe Guy, Kenny Kersey and Kenny Clarke.

title: Minton's Playhouse - Wikipedia
notes: Teddy Hill's house band in 1941: Monk, Joe Guy, Nick Fenton, Kenny Clarke; Christian and Gillespie regular guests; 'the center of the emergence of bebop'.

title: Lee Konitz with Warne Marsh - Wikipedia
notes: Atlantic 1217, recorded 14 June 1955 at Coastal Studios, New York: Konitz, Marsh, Sal Mosca, Billy Bauer, Oscar Pettiford, Kenny Clarke.

title: Jazzmen Detroit - Complete Sessions (Fresh Sound Records FSRCD 645)
notes: Pepper Adams, Kenny Burrell, Tommy Flanagan, Paul Chambers, Kenny Clarke at Rudy Van Gelder's, Hackensack: 30 April and 9 May 1956 (Apothegm, by Adams, on 9 May); first issued on Jazzmen: Detroit, Savoy MG 12083. The liner calls Clarke 'the doyen of contemporary bop drummers'.
